newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer confidence highest since '80s boom-survey.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer confidence highest since '80s boom-survey.

text.p: Consumer confidence has climbed across nearly all areas of Britain to heights not seen since the 1980s, according to a survey published on Tuesday, two days before the election.
"In every region of the UK, except Northern Ireland, people are more optimistic than at any time since the 1980s boom," economic consultancy Business Strategies Ltd said.

The consultancy's previous two surveys, in January and last October, showed consumer confidence buoyant but rising at a slowing rate. Now, it appears it accelerated sharply in the first quarter of the year.

"No one factor explains this renewed upturn," said David Fell, the BSL director responsible for the survey. "A combination of falling unemployment, tax cuts, windfall gains and rising incomes are displacing uncertainties about inflation, interest rates and the outcome of the election."

Prime Minister John Major's Conservative government appears unlikely to reap any electoral reward from the upbeat mood among consumers -- opinion polls show the opposition Labour party well ahead of the Conservatives ahead of Thursday's election.

Of 6,000 consumers surveyed, a positive balance of 20 percent said their financial situation had improved over the past year, and a 19 percent balance expected it to improve further over the next 12 months.
Fell said optimism about household finances was at its highest level this decade while concerns about unemployment were falling "almost as fast as the official figures."
According to the Office for National Statistics, the number of people unemployed and claiming benefit in Britain has dropped by almost half a million to 1.7 million over the year to March.
Fell said the survey did not signal a return to the boom conditions of the last decade.

"These are certainly positive results, but the areas of uncertainty -- on the significance of house prices, on the security of employment, on the windfall gains -- suggest consumers still have their feet on the brake pedal," Fell said.

Over the past three months, the North, the East Midlands, the South West and Wales have seen optimism swell most rapidly.
"The results do not show any discernible North/South or East/West pattern," Fell said.
